reasoning:
When a right triangle is inscribed in a circle, the hypotenuse of the right triangle is the diameter of the circle.

For the 3-4-5 right triangle inscribed in circle Q:
- The hypotenuse is 5, so the diameter of circle Q is 5.
- The radius of circle Q is 5/2.
- The area of circle Q is π(5/2)² = 25π/4.

For the 5-12-13 right triangle inscribed in circle A:
- The hypotenuse is 13, so the diameter of circle A is 13.
- The radius of circle A is 13/2.
- The area of circle A is π(13/2)² = 169π/4.

The ratio of the area of circle Q to the area of circle A is:
(25π/4) / (169π/4) = 25/169

This corresponds to answer choice A.
